newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker but avoids further slide.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker but avoids further slide.

text.p: The slide in the orange juice market skidded to a virtual halt Friday with FCOJ futures ending only slightly down as the failure of freezes to hit the Florida citrus belt continued to weigh on the market, traders said.
"I think we are getting to the point where everyone who wants to be short is short," said Jim Cordier of Allendale Commodities.
Spot January orange juice, reflecting the lack of a nearby freeze threat, ended 1.90 cents weaker at 74.10 cents, a new contract low.
Most active March orange juice settled 0.20 cent weaker at 77.65 cents per pound, traded 78.50 to 77.55 cents, the latter also a new contract low.
Volume was estimated at 2,750 lots compared to Thursday's official 3,945 lots.
Much of the week's losses were due to speculators, who had gambled on freezes hitting the citrus belt, failing to materialise, Cordier said.

The potential for freezes in the belt will wane from the end of January and the market will then focus of demand, which should be spurred by the lower prices, down some 40 percent in recent weeks, Cordier added.
